confirmed.title: Unreviewed draft facts supersede and invalidate approved facts
confirmed.summary: recordFactWithSupersession never checks input.status, so a status="draft" fact (the documented path for untrusted LLM producers, accepted by the /v2/fact schema) that classifies as UPDATE is written and then invalidates approved facts with superseded_by pointing at the unreviewed draft; rejectFact only flips the draft's status and never restores the invalidated approved facts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified by execution: approved fact "John works_at Google" exists; an untrusted producer POSTs /v2/fact {subject John, predicate works_at, object Anthropic, status "draft"} -> decision UPDATE, the approved Google fact gets invalidated_at=now and superseded_by=<draft id>. Reviewer rejects the hallucinated draft -> the approved fact stays permanently invalidated and retrieval demotes it via the contradiction penalty; the vault's current state was corrupted by input the review gate was supposed to fail-closed on. (Side effect of the same missing gate: a draft that duplicates an existing fact returns NONE and is silently never written, so it never even reaches review.)
skeptic_notes: Reproduced the exact failure by executing the real code in a scratch vault. (1) schemas.ts:35 accepts status:"draft" on /v2/fact; api.ts:442 spreads the body (including status) into recordFactWithSupersession. (2) recordFactWithSupersession (layer2-semantic.ts:460-573) never inspects input.status, and classifyOnWrite (layer4-supersession.ts:139) only receives {subject, predicate, object, event_date} — so a draft "John works_at Anthropic" arriving after approved "John works_at Google" classifies UPDATE and the invalidation loop (lines 555-571) stamps the approved fact with invalidated_at and superseded_by=<draft id>. Execution confirmed: draft written with status:"draft", approved fact invalidated. (3) rejectFact (layer2-semantic.ts:155-182) only sets the draft's status to "rejected" and restores nothing — execution confirmed the approved fact stays invalidated after rejection, so getFactsValidAt permanently drops the true fact while the superseder is a rejected record. This bypasses the explicitly fail-closed review gate (api.ts:478-485) and the intended approval-time supersession path /v2/fact/:newId/approve-supersedes/:oldId (api.ts:566-608). The behavior is on neither the DESIGN INTENT nor the KNOWN ISSUES list. The side observation also holds: a draft duplicating an approved fact returns NONE and is never written, so it never enters the review queue. The claim stands; I cannot refute it.

NOT refuted — the claim is verified against the actual source and by live execution. (1) schemas.ts:35 accepts status:"draft" on /v2/fact and README.md:212 documents it as the untrusted-producer path; (2) api.ts:442 passes the body into recordFactWithSupersession with no status gate; (3) layer2-semantic.ts:460-573 never reads input.status, classifyOnWrite is status-blind, and the candidate pre-filter selects approved-only facts, so the invalidation loop at line 555 stamps approved facts with superseded_by=<draft id>; (4) invalidateFact has no status check on the superseder and rejectFact only flips the draft's status — no restore/un-invalidate mechanism exists anywhere in src/. Only the claim's minor side note (duplicate draft → NONE, never reaches review) is narrower than stated: it fires only when the draft matches an approved fact's object and date, which is low-harm; the core critical finding stands.

confirmed.title: Mixed date-only vs full-ISO valid_from breaks same-day supersession; string format decides the winner
confirmed.summary: classifyOnWrite step 4 compares valid_from strings with strict '<' at full length, but the observe path produces date-only valid_from (sanitizeEventDate returns "YYYY-MM-DD", even "YYYY" or "YYYY-MM") while undated facts get full ISO now() — "2026-07-12T07:38:10Z" < "2026-07-12" is false, so a dated contradiction never supersedes a same-day full-ISO fact, defeating exactly the same-day case the v2.14.1 comment claims to fix.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified by execution: 09:00 today an undated doc yields "Mara works_at Google" (valid_from=full ISO now). 10:00 today a doc stating "as of 2026-07-12 Mara works at Anthropic" yields valid_from="2026-07-12" -> decision ADD, Google fact stays current -> two simultaneous current values for a functional predicate, silently. Mirror run confirms the asymmetry: full-ISO new fact DOES supersede a date-only same-day fact, so which fact wins depends on string length/format rather than time or information.

confirmed.title: Duplicate-skip drops the new episode's provenance, permanently starving corroboration and auto fact-check
confirmed.summary: When classifyOnWrite returns NONE (duplicate: same object + same date-prefix), recordFactWithSupersession discards input.derived_from without appending the new episode to the surviving fact (the audit SKIP records record_ids: [] and no evidence chain), so the second independent document leaves no trace; reflection Rule A counts corroboration as the union of derived_from episode IDs across the claim group, so the count stays at 1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified by execution: two different documents ingested the same day both state "TSMC located_in Taiwan" -> second write returns NONE/duplicate and the surviving fact's derived_from is still [doc1] only. Rule A therefore never sees >=2 distinct sources for the claim, corroboration_sources is never annotated, and the auto fact-check pass (which only checks corroborated >=2-source world claims) never verifies it — the system's own "independently stated in 2+ documents" mechanism is silently defeated whenever restatements share a date prefix (the common case: same-day ingests default valid_from to now()).

confirmed.title: findContradictions ignores valid_to, so new facts wrongly invalidate correctly-closed historical facts
confirmed.summary: findContradictions' doc contract requires valid_from/valid_to window overlap but the code never checks valid_to, so a fact that was accurately closed (valid_to in the past) is still returned as a supersession candidate and gets invalidated_at + superseded_by stamped by a non-contradicting new fact.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified by execution: "John works_at Google" valid_from 2020, valid_to 2023-05-31 (correct, ended, approved). New fact "John works_at Anthropic" valid_from 2026 -> UPDATE supersedes the closed Google fact too: it receives invalidated_at=now ("we learned this was wrong" — it never was) and superseded_by=<Anthropic id>. Since facts are never deleted, the false epistemic stamp is permanent, an INVALIDATE audit entry is logged for a correct record, and layer5 retrieval (line 350) applies the contradiction penalty, demoting an accurate piece of employment history in every future query.
skeptic_notes: Reproduced the exact scenario by executing the real code (recordFact with valid_to=2023-05-31, then recordFactWithSupersession with a 2026 fact): the correctly-closed Google fact was returned by findContradictions, classified as UPDATE-superseded, and stamped invalidated_at=now + superseded_by, with an INVALIDATE audit entry. Source verification: findContradictions (layer2-semantic.ts:358-392) checks status/invalidated_at/superseded_by/subject/predicate/object but never valid_to, contradicting its own doc contract at line 344 ("valid_from/valid_to windows overlap"); classifyOnWrite's olderDifferent filter (layer4-supersession.ts:193-200) likewise omits valid_to despite the comment "still current" (line 180); works_at is a functional predicate (line 52) not subject to the person-only location gate; invalidateFact (layer2-semantic.ts:203-230) stamps unconditionally with no valid_to guard. The file header defines invalidated_at as "when WE learned the fact was wrong (epistemic)" — so the stamp is epistemically false for an accurate closed record, is permanent (facts never deleted), and triggers layer5's contradiction penalty (layer5-retrieval.ts:350/358/378: up to 35% multiplier plus a "contradicted (de-ranked)" label) which a merely-closed fact would not receive. The claim is correct and cannot be refuted.
